precise_contribution.answer: The article asserts complete binary sumsets of positive primitive norm values for discriminants -3, -7, -8, -11, with the stated congruence obstructions and exactly the three additional -7 exceptions 7, 77, 203. It also proves stronger split-prime core identities, higher Eisenstein sumsets with sharp universal numbers of summands, and explicit ordered numerical-value pair lower bounds at -7 and -8. The contribution is exact coverage of all eligible targets, rather than merely eventual representation.
precise_contribution.locations: Theorem 1.1, p. 1; Theorem 3.2 and Propositions 3.8-3.9, pp. 4 and 13-14; Theorems 4.1, 5.1, 6.1, pp. 14, 21, 28.
precise_contribution.qualification: This identifies the contribution claimed and supported by the PDF's internal argument. Historical originality and comparison with external literature were not independently established.

conceptual_reason.answer: Primitive numerical norm values are the split-prime semigroup and one ramified dilation. In the Eisenstein case this is P_-3 = A disjoint-union 3A, so only A+A and A+3A need separate binary proofs; 3(A+A) supplies the remaining type. Quaternion norm shells supply candidate pairs; orbit averaging and a precisely normalized Hecke bound control inert-prime losses. Exact dyadic and ramified filters preserve a positive margin. Finite scans, rational interval inequalities, and split-factor descent then convert effective existence into complete classifications.
conceptual_reason.locations: Opening explanation, pp. 1-2; Proposition 3.1, p. 4; Sections 3.3-3.6, pp. 6-12; reusable mechanism in Appendix B, pp. 34-35.
conceptual_reason.focus_check: The identity is displayed on p. 1 beside the opening classification, explained on p. 2, and proved elementarily in Proposition 3.1 on p. 4 before the norm-shell counting in Section 3.2 on p. 5. The proof establishes both directions and disjointness, including exclusion of inert primes, at most one ramified factor, and coprime coordinates for constructed values.

hardest_step_and_proof_location.answer: The deepest imported input is Lemma 2.1 (pp. 3-4): the all-integral-ideal Hecke normalization, removal of global norm characters, and weight-two spectral bound. For the central Eisenstein argument, the most delicate arithmetic step is the six-point ramified quotient and exact mixed-family obstruction count in Sections 3.4.3-3.4.4 (pp. 9-10), which is combined with the odd-component filter and the strict sieve bound in Section 3.6 (pp. 11-12). Across the later cases, the joint ramified/inert correlation at -7 (Section 4.3, pp. 16-17) and preservation of all ideal classes with inverse-unit mass at -11 (Sections 6.1-6.2, pp. 29-30) are material places where normalization affects the conclusion.
hardest_step_and_proof_location.proof_organization: The Eisenstein argument is grouped in the single central Section 3, pp. 4-14: arithmetic preliminaries, counting, local filters, numerical estimates, finite completion, then primitive and higher sumsets. The common spectral input remains separately stated in Section 2, and Appendix A states the finite certificates' proof role.

limits.answer: The theorems concern positive numerical values, with zero coordinates and signs allowed and without counting different coordinate representations as different summands. Only four discriminants are covered. The paper uses deep classical spectral results and computer-assisted finite assertions; it does not give a wholly elementary or computation-free proof. The small anchor menus are finite-range devices, and Proposition 3.7 proves that a fixed finite Eisenstein menu cannot work globally. Appendix C's balanced Eisenstein classification remains a question: its two finite failures 8 and 44 below 10^8 are not promoted to an all-target theorem.
limits.locations: Definition and value convention, p. 1; Proposition 3.7, p. 13; Appendix A, pp. 32-34; Appendix C, p. 35.
